name: amp_branch_create
description:
Fork a branch in a cluster — a zero-copy, copy-on-write clone of the data.

Use when the user asks to **branch**, **fork**, or **clone** a database so
sub-agents can work on isolated copies in parallel.

cluster_id.description: UUID of the cluster to branch. Use ``amp_cluster_list``.

parent_branch_id.description:
Branch to fork from. Omit to fork the cluster's default
branch ("main").

fork_point_lsn.description:
Ancestor LSN to fork at ("X/X" hex). Omit for the
parent's latest; required when the parent has no running compute the
controller can read the flush LSN from.

datapack_id.description: UUID of the datapack. Defaults to the active datapack.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

name: amp_cluster_create
description:
Create a cluster (a Postgres database) in a datapack.

Use when the user asks to **create**, **provision**, or **spin up** a
database/cluster. The datapack's AMP shared pool is created automatically on
the first cluster; a default branch named "main" is created with the cluster.

Two shapes:

- Default (``with_writer=False``): the cluster only — no compute. Add an
  endpoint afterwards with ``amp_compute_create``.
- ``with_writer=True``: one task also provisions a ``read_write`` endpoint
  on the ``main`` branch, sized by ``cpu``/``memory`` — a ready-to-connect
  database (what the UI wizard creates). When omitted, cpu/memory default
  to 0.5 vCPU / 4Gi (sized to fit the free tier); tell the user the
  default was applied and offer a different size. This shape reserves
  compute, so the account's tier vCPU cap applies (defaults: free 0.5 /
  standard 2 / pro 5 vCPU across all datapacks, deployment-tunable;
  enterprise uncapped) — exceeding it returns a 402 with a
  ``*_TIER_CORE_LIMIT`` code. Check remaining budget first with
  ``amp_core_budget``; on a limit error tell the user their tier's cap
  (or size down) instead of retrying.

datapack_id.description:
UUID of the datapack. If omitted, the caller's active
datapack is used. Use ``datapack_search(query=...)`` to look one up.

pg_version.description:
Optional Postgres major version. Omit to take AMP's default;
only the default version is currently accepted.

with_writer.description:
Also provision the ``main``-branch ``read_write`` endpoint
in the same task. Default False (cluster only).

cpu.description:
Endpoint CPU reservation, a Kubernetes quantity (e.g. "2",
"500m"). Only used with ``with_writer=True``; omit for the
0.5-vCPU default.

memory.description:
Endpoint memory reservation (e.g. "8Gi"). Only used with
``with_writer=True``. Omit to derive it from ``cpu`` at AMP's
required 8 GiB per vCPU (4Gi at the 0.5-vCPU default).

password.description:
cloud_admin password for the writer (``with_writer=True``
only). Omit and a strong one is generated and returned once as
``cloud_admin_password`` — the control plane keeps only the SCRAM
verifier, so it cannot be recovered later. Printable ASCII, 8-128.

connectivity_mode.description:
exposure of the ``with_writer`` endpoint.
``ingress_external`` gives it a public address on the shared ingress load
balancer so a client OUTSIDE the cluster can connect; omit for the
in-cluster default. Only used with ``with_writer=True``, and it is a
create-time choice — it cannot be changed afterwards, so decide it now.
Requires ``allowed_cidrs``.

allowed_cidrs.description:
source IP allow-list for ``ingress_external`` (CIDRs, each with
an explicit prefix, e.g. ``["203.0.113.4/32"]``). REQUIRED when
``connectivity_mode`` is ``ingress_external``. **Ask the user for the IP(s)
to allow** — a public endpoint with no allow-list is refused, and so is any
entry broader than /24 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6), an unspecified/default
network, or an IPv4-mapped IPv6 range.

extensions.description: Optional catalog extensions to seed on the default branch.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

name: amp_compute_create
description:
Provision a compute instance (an endpoint) on a branch.

Use when the user asks to **create**, **provision**, or **attach** compute /
an endpoint so a branch is reachable. A branch admits at most one
``read_write`` compute instance.

Adding an endpoint reserves compute, so the account's tier vCPU cap
applies (defaults: free 0.5 / standard 2 / pro 5 vCPU across all
datapacks, deployment-tunable; enterprise uncapped) — exceeding it
returns a 402 with a ``*_TIER_CORE_LIMIT`` code. Check remaining budget
first with ``amp_core_budget``; on a limit error tell the user their
tier's cap (or size down) instead of retrying.

cluster_id.description: UUID of the cluster. Use ``amp_cluster_list`` to find it.

branch_id.description: UUID of the branch. Use ``amp_branch_list`` to find it.

cpu.description:
CPU reservation, a Kubernetes quantity (e.g. "2", "1500m"). Omit
for the 0.5-vCPU default (sized to fit the free tier); tell the
user the default was applied and offer a different size.

memory.description:
Memory reservation (e.g. "8Gi"). Omit to derive it from
``cpu`` at AMP's required 8 GiB per vCPU (4Gi at the 0.5-vCPU
default); a memory-only call derives ``cpu`` from it the same way.

password.description:
cloud_admin password for a ``read_write`` endpoint. Omit it and
a strong one is generated and returned once as ``cloud_admin_password``
— the control plane keeps only the verifier, so it cannot be recovered
later. A ``read_only`` endpoint takes no password. MEKO-1017 handling:
a FORK's writer (``password_required: false``) reuses the parent
branch's password — no password is set or returned, any you pass is
dropped, and a ``password_notice`` is returned instead. CAVEAT:
``password_required`` is root-only, so a SECOND writer on a ROOT branch
(a deleted-and-recreated writer) still reports true and still gets a
generated password — but the controller keeps the root's ORIGINAL one,
so that generated password won't log in. The tool can't detect this; if
the database already existed, tell the user to use its original
cloud_admin password. An older api_server that doesn't report
``password_required`` (or a failed branch lookup) also generates, so
the first writer of a root is never regressed.

connectivity_mode.description:
``ingress_external`` to give the endpoint a public
address on the shared ingress load balancer so a client outside
the cluster can connect. Omit for the in-cluster default. Requires
``allowed_cidrs``.

allowed_cidrs.description:
source IP allow-list for ``ingress_external`` (CIDRs, each
with an explicit prefix, e.g. ``["203.0.113.4/32"]``). REQUIRED when
``connectivity_mode`` is ``ingress_external`` — a public endpoint with no
allow-list is open to the whole internet behind only the password, so
Meko rejects it, along with any entry broader than /24 (IPv4) or /48
(IPv6), an unspecified/default network, or an IPv4-mapped IPv6 range.
Ask the user for the IPs to allow.

datapack_id.description: UUID of the datapack. Defaults to the active datapack.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

name: amp_compute_resize
description:
Resize a compute instance (endpoint) — change its CPU and/or memory.

Use when the user asks to **resize**, **scale**, or change the
**CPU/memory** of an endpoint. At least one of ``cpu`` / ``memory`` is
required; an omitted field keeps its current value (no defaults are
filled in — unlike the create tools). Blocks until the AMP task
completes. AMP requires 8 GiB of memory per vCPU, so growing cpu
usually means growing memory in the same call.

Growing CPU counts against the account's tier vCPU cap (defaults: free
0.5 / standard 2 / pro 5 vCPU across all datapacks, deployment-tunable;
enterprise uncapped) — exceeding it returns a 402 with a
``*_TIER_CORE_LIMIT`` code. Check
remaining budget first with ``amp_core_budget``; on a limit error tell
the user their tier's cap (or size down) instead of retrying.
Memory-only resizes never hit the cap.

cluster_id.description: UUID of the cluster. Use ``amp_cluster_list`` to find it.

branch_id.description: UUID of the branch. Use ``amp_branch_list`` to find it.

compute_id.description: UUID of the compute instance. Use ``amp_compute_list``.

cpu.description: New CPU reservation, a Kubernetes quantity (e.g. "2", "500m").

datapack_id.description: UUID of the datapack. Defaults to the active datapack.

Get the account's AMP vCPU budget: cores used across ALL datapacks vs the

Use BEFORE proposing a sized operation (``amp_cluster_create`` with

when the user asks how much compute they have left. Read-only.

datapack_id.description:
UUID of the datapack (routes the request; the budget
itself is account-wide). Defaults to the active datapack.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

name: artifact_get
description:
Retrieve a previously uploaded artifact by its content hash.

Use this when the agent needs to read back a file it (or another agent)
previously stored via artifact_put.

Small files (< 1 MB): content is returned inline as content_base64.
Large files (>= 1 MB): the file is written to ~/.meko/artifacts/<hash>/<filename>
on the local machine and local_path is returned. The agent should read the
file from that path using normal file-reading tools.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id for trace nesting.

datapack_id.description: Datapack UUID. Defaults to the caller's default datapack.

agent_id.description: Agent identifier for trace attribution.

name: artifact_put
description:
Upload a file artifact to this datapack.

Use this when an agent has generated a file (report, CSV, PDF, code output,
etc.) and wants to persist it in Meko for later retrieval or cross-agent
sharing. To make a file's content searchable by meaning instead, use
knowledgebase_upload_document.

Files smaller than 1 MB are stored inline in the database.
Files 1 MB or larger are stored in the datapack's S3 bucket.
Uploading the same bytes twice is idempotent — returns the existing artifact.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id for trace nesting.

datapack_id.description: Target datapack UUID. Defaults to the caller's default datapack.

agent_id.description: Agent identifier for trace attribution.

name: context_search
description:
One retrieval call across the conversation cache, memory, and the
knowledgebase — queries every source ``force_source`` allows **in
parallel** and returns each one's results in its own labeled bucket.
Nothing here suppresses another source: a conversation-cache hit no
longer hides a KB document that supersedes it, and a "good enough"
memory no longer skips the KB either. Any source can legitimately come
back empty — that means nothing relevant, not a broken call.

Each source's own floor:
  - Conversation: CONVERSATION_HIT_DISTANCE gates the cache lookup
    itself (unchanged).
  - Memory: no absolute floor on the ``auto`` path. The public
    ``memory_search`` tool applies the runtime ``memory_search_min_score``
    floor because it answers from memory alone; on the ``auto`` path
    this call keeps the full mem0 list because the KB and conversation
    buckets sit beside it and let the caller discount a weak row. That
    preserves hits whose BM25 or entity signal is strong and whose
    cosine is weak, which a dense floor would veto. The cost is that
    this bucket can be non-empty for a query with nothing relevant in
    memory, and nothing absorbs that when the other two sources come
    back empty. When ``force_source="memory"`` skips the other two
    sources entirely, this path reapplies the same runtime floor,
    because memory is then the sole bucket and there is nothing to
    discount against.
  - Knowledge base: CONTEXT_SEARCH_KB_MAX_DISTANCE, new here.
    knowledgebase_search's own trim is relative-to-the-top-match only
    and always keeps at least one result by design, so this adds the
    absolute cutoff that lets a genuinely irrelevant query return zero
    KB chunks instead of one weak one.

Set ``force_source`` to query only one source instead of all three —
``"conversation"``, ``"memory"``, or ``"knowledge_base"`` skip the other
two entirely (not just filter them from the response), for a caller
that already knows which source it wants. ``memory_search`` /
``knowledgebase_search`` remain available directly too, for UUID
lookups this tool doesn't surface.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find.

conversation_id.description: Conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

agent_id.description: Agent identifier scoping memory/conversation lookups.

datapack_id.description: UUID of the datapack to search within.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return per source (default 10).

prompt.description:
Optional. What the user asked, when ``query`` is a rewrite of
it. Recorded in the datapack's search log; it does not change
the search.

verify.description:
Optional, default false. A replay of a saved search: it is
recorded in the event log marked verify, and is not counted in the
owner's search log, daily counts or token-savings statistics, but it
counts against the user's search limit like any other search. It
returns the normal result. Only the Meko api_server's replay is
honoured; from any other caller the argument is ignored and the
search is logged and counted like a normal one. Leave it off for a
real question.

conversation_hit_distance.description:
Optional, default unset. A cosine-distance
cutoff from 0 to 2 that replaces ``CONVERSATION_HIT_DISTANCE`` for
the conversation source of this call only. Unset keeps the server's
configured gate. Raising it lets weaker turns count as hits, so more
questions get conversation context (2.0 admits every candidate) and
more verbatim turns are sent. The reported token_savings use a flat
per-hit estimate, so they do not reflect those extra tokens. Ignored when
``force_source`` leaves the conversation source out.

name: conversation_add_message
description:
Add a message (user prompt + assistant response) to a conversation.

Call after ``conversation_create`` to append each message. A message
represents one interaction: the user's input and the assistant's
output, stored as a span inside the conversation's trace. The turn
is queued for background writing and the tool returns immediately
with the assigned message ID.

conversation_id.description: UUID returned by ``conversation_create``.

agent_id.description:
Agent identifier. Must match the ``agent_id`` used in
``conversation_create``.

reasoning.description:
Optional short paragraph (1–3 sentences) explaining
the *why* behind the reply. Plain text; inline markdown
allowed.

metadata.description: Optional JSON string of arbitrary metadata to attach.

seed.description:
Optional seed string for deterministic message ID. When
both a hook and the MCP server use the same seed, they
produce the same message ID, enabling deduplication.

datapack_id.description:
UUID of the datapack whose Langfuse project stores
the message. Required whenever no server-side default
resolves for the caller. Use ``datapack_search(query=...)`` to look up
the id. Calls without ``datapack_id`` and without a resolved
default return ``{"error": "datapack_id_required"}`` and
persist nothing.

plan.description:
Optional list of 2–4 imperative, single-sentence actions
taken for this turn. Pass a list of strings; do not
pre-number entries.

name: conversation_create
description:
Create a new conversation to store a chat / dialog exchange.

Invoke when the user asks to **store**, **save**, or **log a
conversation**, **chat history**, or **query and response**. Creates
a conversation container; use ``conversation_add_message`` to append
each user-prompt / assistant-response pair.

agent_id.description:
Agent identifier. Conversations are scoped per agent.
Use a consistent ID across calls for the same agent. Coding
agents use ``<client>:<repo-basename>`` (e.g.
``claude_code:myrepo``); other clients use a stable client
name (e.g. ``claude_desktop``).

title.description: Optional human-readable title for the conversation.

metadata.description: Optional JSON string of arbitrary metadata to attach.

session_id.description:
Optional session ID used as the conversation-container
dedup key. When supplied it is HONORED so callers that derive a
stable id (e.g. a Codex rollout basename) reconnect the same
conversation instead of creating a duplicate. If omitted, a new
UUID is generated. Non-hex ids are normalized deterministically
into a valid 32-hex Langfuse trace id (same seed -> same id), so
the returned conversation ``id`` may differ from the raw input
while still deduplicating consistently across callers.

datapack_id.description:
UUID of the datapack whose Langfuse project stores
the conversation. Required whenever no server-side default
resolves for the caller. Use ``datapack_search(query=...)`` to look up
the id. Calls without ``datapack_id`` and without a resolved
default return ``{"error": "datapack_id_required"}`` and
persist nothing.

name: conversation_delete
description:
Permanently delete a conversation and all its messages.

This is a hard delete — the conversation and all associated traces
are removed from Langfuse. This cannot be undone. Only deletes if
the conversation belongs to the specified agent.

conversation_id.description: UUID of the conversation to delete.

agent_id.description:
Agent identifier. Only deletes if the conversation
belongs to this agent.

datapack_id.description:
UUID of the datapack whose Langfuse project holds
the conversation. Required whenever no server-side default
resolves for the caller. Use ``datapack_search(query=...)`` to look up
the id. Calls without ``datapack_id`` and without a resolved
default return ``{"error": "datapack_id_required"}``.

name: conversation_get
description:
Retrieve a stored conversation by ID, optionally including its turns.

Use this when the user asks to **recall**, **retrieve**, or **review** a
previously stored conversation or chat history. By default returns only
metadata and message count. Set ``include_messages=True`` to fetch the
full message history with input, output, and reasoning.

conversation_id.description: UUID of the conversation to fetch.

agent_id.description:
Agent identifier. Only returns the conversation if it
belongs to this agent.

include_messages.description:
Set True to include the full message history
(input, output, reasoning). Default False returns metadata only.

limit.description: Max number of messages to return (default 100).

datapack_id.description:
UUID of the datapack whose Langfuse project holds
the conversation. Required whenever no server-side default
resolves for the caller. Use ``datapack_search(query=...)`` to look up
the id. Calls without ``datapack_id`` and without a resolved
default return ``{"error": "datapack_id_required"}``.

name: conversation_list
description:
List stored conversations for a datapack, ordered by most recently updated.

Use this when the user asks to **list**, **show**, or **browse** the
stored conversations or chat history for a datapack.

agent_id.description: Agent identifier (used for trace attribution only).

limit.description: Max number of conversations to return (default 20).

offset.description: Number of conversations to skip for pagination (default 0).

conversation_id.description:
Optional. Pass the active conversation_id to nest
the list-call's trace under it, or omit — listing does not
depend on a specific conversation. When omitted, the call gets
its own ephemeral trace session so it still appears in Langfuse
but is not falsely attributed to an unrelated conversation.

datapack_id.description:
UUID of the datapack whose conversations to list. If
omitted, the caller's default datapack is used. Use
``datapack_search(query=...)`` to look up the id.

name: conversation_update
description: Update a conversation's title and/or metadata.

conversation_id.description: UUID of the conversation to update.

agent_id.description:
Agent identifier. Only updates if the conversation
belongs to this agent.

title.description: New title (pass to change, omit to keep).

metadata.description: New metadata as a JSON string (pass to replace, omit to keep).

datapack_id.description:
UUID of the datapack whose Langfuse project holds
the conversation. Required whenever no server-side default
resolves for the caller. Use ``datapack_search(query=...)`` to look up
the id. Calls without ``datapack_id`` and without a resolved
default return ``{"error": "datapack_id_required"}``.

name: datapack_create
description:
Create a new Meko datapack — an isolated database environment with its
own agent namespace.

Use this when the user asks to **create**, **provision**, or **set up**
a new datapack or workspace.

This is a Meko platform operation. Direct SQL access against the
underlying database is not part of the published MCP surface; use the
Meko control plane (UI or REST) for schema and data work that needs
raw queries.

name.description: Name for the new datapack.  Must be unique across the platform.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

datapack_id.description: Optional UUID of a datapack for Langfuse project routing.

folder_id.description:
Optional UUID of a project folder to file the new datapack
into. Only deployments with the Projects feature have folders; on
any other deployment passing one is refused, so omit it unless
the project tools are in your tool list. Where it does apply, it
saves a second call to ``project_add_datapack``, ``project_describe``
finds the id, and the folder is checked before the datapack is
created so a wrong id creates nothing. Omit it and the datapack is
created Unfiled, which works exactly as it always has.

name: datapack_delete
description:
Permanently delete a Meko datapack, dropping its database and all roles.

Use this when the user asks to **delete**, **destroy**, or **remove**
a datapack.  This is irreversible — the database and all data are dropped.

datapack_id.description:
UUID of the datapack to delete. Required — there is no
default to avoid deleting the wrong datapack. Use ``datapack_search(query=...)``
to look up the id.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

name: datapack_describe
description:
Describe a Meko datapack by id, optionally including status info.

Use this when the user asks to **describe**, **get details**, or **inspect**
a specific datapack.  Set ``include_status=True`` to also retrieve agent
count, knowledge base count, and provisioning status.

The returned JSON exposes count fields aligned with the Meko UI's
Datapack Constructs diagram:

- ``memory_count``: total memories stored for the datapack (mem0).
- ``collective_memory_count``: memories promoted into shared knowledge
  (UI label: "Collective Memories").
- ``learnings_count``: memories awaiting a promotion decision.
- ``knowledge_base_file_count``: KB documents indexed or being indexed
  (UI label: "Knowledge Base"). ``null`` if the datapack status endpoint
  is unreachable, the api-server is too old to report it, or the
  api-server couldn't count the documents.
- ``knowledge_chunk_count``: RAG chunks across all KB documents. Not a
  user-facing metric — surfaced for debugging RAG behavior.
- ``shared_knowledge_count``: ``collective_memory_count +
  knowledge_base_file_count`` (UI label: "Shared Knowledge"). ``null``
  if ``knowledge_base_file_count`` is ``null``.

Deprecated:

- ``knowledge_count``: **deprecated** alias of
  ``knowledge_chunk_count``. Preserved for backward compatibility so
  existing consumers keep working; carries the same value. New callers
  should read ``knowledge_chunk_count``. The alias is scheduled for
  removal in a future major/breaking release; that removal will be
  called out separately.

datapack_id.description:
UUID of the datapack to describe. If omitted, the caller's
default datapack is used. Use ``datapack_search(query=...)`` to look up the id.

include_status.description:
Set True to also fetch agent_count, knowledge_base_count,
and provisioning status. Default False. ``knowledge_base_count`` is
the number of knowledge bases (always 1), not a file count; read
``knowledge_base_file_count`` for files.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

name: datapack_list
description:
List the Meko datapacks visible to the current user.

Use this when the user asks to **list**, **show**, or **view all**
datapacks, workspaces, or environments. To find one datapack's id by
name, call ``datapack_search(query=...)`` instead: it is paged and works
for accounts of any size.

With no ``query`` and no ``limit`` this returns every datapack, up to
``DATAPACK_LIST_MAX_UNFILTERED`` (default 1000). Above that it returns
``{"error": "too_many_datapacks"}``; use ``datapack_search`` then.

With ``query`` and no ``limit`` this returns every match, up to 100.
When more than 100 datapacks match, it returns ``too_many_datapacks``.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

datapack_id.description: Optional UUID of a datapack for Langfuse project routing.

query.description: Optional case-insensitive substring of the datapack name.

limit.description:
Optional maximum number of rows, capped at 100. With ``limit``
the result is the first ``limit`` matches and does not say
whether more exist; ``datapack_search`` returns ``has_more``.

name: datapack_search
description:
Search the Meko datapacks visible to the current user, one page at a time.

Use this to **find a datapack's id**, to show the user some datapacks to
choose from, or to browse an account with many datapacks. It works for
accounts of any size; prefer it over ``datapack_list``.

- Find a datapack by part of its name: ``query="acme"``.
- Find a datapack by its exact name: ``name="Acme Prod"``.
- Next page: pass the previous result's ``next_cursor`` as ``cursor``,
  with the same ``query``, ``name``, ``grant`` and ``sort``. An empty
  ``next_cursor`` means there are no more pages you can fetch; if
  ``has_more`` is still true, narrow the search with ``query``.
- Set ``include_total=True`` only when you must show "N of M"; it costs
  an extra count.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring of the datapack name (max 200 chars).

limit.description: Rows per page, 1-100 (default 20). Out-of-range values are clamped.

cursor.description: ``next_cursor`` from the previous page. Empty for the first page.

grant.description:
``owner`` (datapacks you own), ``shared`` (shared with you), or
empty for both.

include_total.description: Also return how many datapacks match, in ``total``.

datapack_id.description: Optional UUID of a datapack for Langfuse project routing.

name: datapack_update
description:
Update a Meko datapack's name, description, and/or conversation-search
opt-out.

Use this when the user asks to **rename**, **update**, or **change the
description of** a datapack, or to **opt out of** (or back into)
conversation-history search. ``name``, ``description``, and
``conversation_search_opt_out`` are all optional; at least one must be
provided. If none are provided the tool returns ``nothing_to_update``
without calling the Meko API.

Conversation-history search is enabled by default for every datapack —
pass ``conversation_search_opt_out=True`` to stop future conversation
turns from being embedded into the search cache for this datapack, or
``False`` to re-enable. This never touches turns already embedded.

Empty strings are treated as "not provided" — passing ``description=""``
will NOT clear an existing description; that operation is not supported
via MCP.

datapack_id.description:
UUID of the datapack to update. Use ``datapack_search(query=...)`` to
look up the id.

conversation_search_opt_out.description:
True to stop indexing this datapack's
future conversation turns for search; False to re-enable. Optional.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

name: knowledgebase_delete_document
description:
Permanently delete ONE knowledge-base file (document) from a datapack.
This cannot be undone: the document's chunks and metadata are removed in
one transaction; deletion of the stored file itself is BEST-EFFORT — the
response's ``s3_deleted`` says whether it happened, so report honestly
when it is false (chunks gone, stored file possibly still present).

Use ONLY when the user explicitly asks to delete/remove a knowledge-base
file, and confirm with them before calling. Obtain ``document_id`` from
``knowledgebase_search`` hits (each hit carries ``document_id``; hits do
NOT carry a filename) — never guess an id. When confirming, echo the id
and the matched chunk text; the authoritative filename list is the
platform's documents API / the Meko UI, not search hits.

Errors carry the HTTP ``status``: 403 (not the datapack owner, a
maintainer, or the file's uploader — report and stop), 409 with code
``DOCUMENT_PROCESSING`` (still indexing — wait for it to finish, then
retry), 404 (no such document in this datapack).

document_id.description: UUID of the document to delete.

conversation_id.description: UUID from conversation_create, for trace nesting.

datapack_id.description:
UUID of the datapack. If omitted, the caller's active
datapack is used.

name: knowledgebase_document_status
description:
Check the upload and indexing status of a file previously uploaded via
knowledgebase_upload_document.

Poll this with the `key` from knowledgebase_upload_document's response,
passed here as document_key, until state reaches a terminal value.
Poll every 10-30 seconds; indexing a large PDF can take minutes.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id for trace nesting.

datapack_id.description: Datapack UUID. Defaults to the caller's default datapack.

agent_id.description: Agent identifier for trace attribution.

name: knowledgebase_search
description:
Hybrid search across the knowledgebase.

Invoke when the user asks to **search**, **find**, or **look up**
information in their knowledgebase or uploaded documents. Combines
semantic vector similarity with keyword full-text search over the
``datapacks.knowledge_bases`` table; each result is tagged with a
``match_type`` of ``"semantic"``, ``"keyword"``, or ``"hybrid"``.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find.

conversation_id.description: Conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

datapack_id.description: UUID of the datapack to search within.

agent_id.description: Agent identifier scoping the search.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default 10).

skip_conversation.description:
Deprecated, no-op. Conversation-history checking
was removed from this tool; this parameter is kept only so
existing callers (e.g. the inference gateway's "Regenerate with
full search" flow) don't break while they migrate off it.

name: knowledgebase_upload_document
description:
Request a presigned S3 URL for uploading a file to this datapack's
Knowledge Base.

Use this when the file's content should be searchable later: docs,
manuals, policies or notes that people or agents will ask questions
about. The file is chunked and indexed, and its passages come back from
knowledgebase_search and context_search. To keep a file exactly as-is
and fetch it back whole (a generated report, a result CSV), use
artifact_put instead. If it is not clear whether the user needs
semantic search or whole-file retrieval, ask.

Before calling this, check that you can send the file's bytes in an
HTTPS POST yourself. You need the bytes and a shell or code tool; with
one, run `curl -sS -o /dev/null -m 10 -w '%{http_code}' https://s3.amazonaws.com`.
Any HTTP status means you can reach S3; a connection, DNS or proxy error
means you can't. If you have no shell or code tool, or the check fails,
don't call this: the URL can't be used, and on a free or standard account
the request holds the file's size against the storage quota for up to 15
minutes. Point the user to the Cloud UI's Add Knowledge instead.

This tool does not touch the file's bytes — it only asks api_server for
somewhere to put them. To upload, POST the file directly to the returned
`url` as multipart/form-data: every key in `fields` as a form field (in
order), then the file's bytes as the last field, named "file". With curl:

    curl -F key=<fields.key> -F policy=<fields.policy> ... \
         -F file=@/local/path/to/report.pdf <url>

(repeat -F for every key in `fields`, in the order given, file last). A
background watcher notices the object once it lands in S3 and registers
and indexes it; no follow-up call is needed. Poll
knowledgebase_document_status with this response's `key` as its
`document_key` to track progress.

The URL accepts only a body of exactly `size` bytes whose SHA-256 is
`content_hash`, for 5 minutes. If S3 answers 400 EntityTooSmall or
EntityTooLarge, `size` was wrong: call this tool again with the right
size and upload through the new URL. The earlier URL can never succeed
and expires on its own.

filename/size/content_hash are validated before api_server is called, so
a bad request fails at once with VALIDATION_ERROR. content_head_base64 is
required (content_head_base64_required when missing) and is sniffed
against the extension before a URL is issued. Send the file's first 3072
bytes, or the whole file if it is shorter: a sample shorter than that, or
longer than `size`, is rejected as VALIDATION_ERROR, since it means `size`
is wrong. Text files must be UTF-8, since indexing reads nothing else. The
sniff only catches obvious mismatches early (a renamed file); api_server
checks the stored bytes again regardless.

If identical content (by SHA-256) is already in this datapack, the
response has already_uploaded=true, an empty url and no fields: nothing
needs uploading. If that file's indexing never started or failed, asking
again queues it again.

On a free or standard account, an issued URL holds its `size` against the
storage quota until the file is registered, or for up to 15 minutes if it
is never uploaded. FREE_TIER_KB_STORAGE_LIMIT /
STANDARD_TIER_KB_STORAGE_LIMIT (status 402) mean there is no room: tell
the user to free space or upgrade rather than retrying.

Accepted file types (by extension): .pdf, .txt, .text, .md, .json, .csv,
.xml, .html, .htm. Maximum size per file: 5 MB on Free, 50 MB on
Standard, 60 MB on Pro and above (VALIDATION_ERROR when larger).

size.description: The file's exact size in bytes.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 hex digest of the file's bytes (e.g. `sha256sum` locally).

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id for trace nesting.

content_head_base64.description:
Base64 of the file's first 3072 bytes (the whole
           file if shorter). Required.

datapack_id.description: Target datapack UUID. Defaults to the caller's default datapack.

agent_id.description: Agent identifier for trace attribution.

name: memory_add
description:
Store a fact as a long-term memory.

Invoke when the caller has an explicit fact to persist: the user has
asked to save something, the fact appears only in the assistant's
output or a tool result, or a prior stored memory must be overwritten
with a correction.

Memories are stored in a pgvector collection; mem0 also links each
memory to the named entities it mentions (people, projects, tools) in
a companion entity-store collection, which boosts later searches that
name those entities.

text.description: Plain text content to store as a memory.

conversation_id.description:
UUID from ``conversation_create``. Required for
trace nesting.

agent_id.description:
Agent identifier. Determines which isolated
vector collection the memory is stored in. Coding agents use
``<client>:<repo-basename>`` (e.g. ``claude_code:myrepo``);
other clients use a stable client name (e.g.
``claude_desktop``); omit for the cross-project
``meko_agent`` bucket.

run_id.description:
Optional. Langfuse **trace metadata only** — it is attached
as a trace tag and is NOT persisted on the memory row, so it
does not scope the write and cannot be used to retrieve it. The
row's filterable conversation tag comes from
``conversation_id`` alone; to read these memories back with a
conversation filter, pass that ``conversation_id`` as
``memory_search(run_id=…)``.

metadata.description: Optional JSON string of arbitrary metadata to attach.

messages.description:
Optional JSON string of conversation history as a list
of ``{"role": "...", "content": "..."}`` objects. When
provided, this is used instead of wrapping ``text`` as a
single user message.

name: memory_delete_all
description:
Permanently delete memories. This cannot be undone.

Deletes every memory that matches ALL of: this ``agent_id``, the calling
user, this ``datapack_id``, and, when given, this ``run_id``. Other agents'
and other users' memories in the datapack are never touched.

Two defaults widen or move the target without saying so in the call:
an omitted ``agent_id`` means the ``meko_agent`` bucket, and an omitted
``datapack_id`` means your default datapack. The response's ``scope``
echoes the values actually used.

conversation_id.description: UUID from conversation_create, for trace nesting.

agent_id.description:
Agent identifier whose memories to delete. Defaults to
``meko_agent``.

run_id.description:
Optional. Narrows the delete to rows tagged with this
`meko_conversation_id`. Normalized the same way as
`memory_search(run_id=…)`, so a search preview and this delete
target the same rows. Must be a conversation id (32 lowercase hex
chars, hyphens optional); anything else returns `invalid_run_id`
rather than falling back to deleting every memory for the agent.

datapack_id.description:
Datapack to delete from. Defaults to your default
datapack. A stdio server has no default, so pass it there.

name: memory_delete_by_id
description: Permanently delete a single memory by its UUID. This cannot be undone.

memory_id.description:
UUID of the memory to delete. Obtain from the ``id`` field
returned by memory_search or memory_get_all.

conversation_id.description: UUID from conversation_create, for trace nesting.

agent_id.description:
Agent identifier whose memory store contains this memory.
Must match the writer's `agent_id`.

name: memory_get_all
description:
List memories for the current datapack, one page at a time.

Each call returns one page plus ``total`` and ``total_pages``. To read
every memory, call again with ``page`` = 2, 3, ... up to ``total_pages``.

conversation_id.description: UUID from conversation_create, for trace nesting.

agent_id.description:
Agent identifier, used for trace attribution. NOTE: this
listing is scoped by datapack + user, not filtered by agent_id, so
it returns memories written by any client. For naming, coding
agents use "<client>:<repo-basename>", Claude Desktop uses
"claude_desktop".

run_id.description: Optional run identifier (ignored, kept for backward compatibility).

promoted.description:
If True, return promoted memories (GET /promoted-memories).
If False (default), return regular memories (GET /memories).

page_size.description:
Optional rows per page. Defaults to 20; the server caps it
at 100, and the response's ``page_size`` shows the value used.

name: memory_get_by_id
description: Retrieve a single memory by its UUID.

memory_id.description:
UUID of the memory to fetch. Obtain from the ``id`` field
returned by memory_search or memory_get_all — must be a valid UUID,
not an arbitrary string.

conversation_id.description: UUID from conversation_create, for trace nesting.

agent_id.description: Agent identifier whose memory store contains this memory.

name: memory_promote
description:
Promote memories into the datapack's shared knowledge base.

Moves each memory out of the agent's private mem0 store into the tenant
knowledge base + promoted collection, then evicts it
from mem0 — a one-way action. Only datapack owners and maintainers may
promote; viewers and contributors get a permission error (403 FORBIDDEN).

conversation_id.description: UUID from conversation_create, for trace nesting.

memory_ids.description:
UUIDs to promote. Obtain from the ``id`` field returned by
memory_search or memory_get_all — must be valid UUIDs, not an
arbitrary string.

agent_id.description: Agent identifier whose memories these are.

datapack_id.description: Target datapack. Defaults to the caller's default datapack.

name: memory_search
description:
Hybrid search across stored memories.

Combines semantic (vector) similarity with keyword matching and an
entity boost: memories that mention the specific things named in the
query (people, projects, tools) rank higher. Returns matching
memories under a "results" key.

Results below the runtime ``memory_search_min_score`` setting (mem0's
raw, unfused cosine-similarity value — see _sufficiency_score — default
0.2, NOT the fused hybrid score results are ranked by) are dropped as
weak matches rather than returned. A query with no memory above that
floor can legitimately return an empty ``results`` list even when
``limit`` allowed more. Only this tool applies the floor. It answers from one
bucket, so a weak hit becomes the answer. ``context_search`` calls the
underlying mem0 search directly and keeps the unfiltered list, because
its KB and conversation buckets sit beside the memory one and let the
caller discount a weak row.

query.description: Natural language description of what to find.

conversation_id.description:
Used purely for Langfuse trace nesting (so the
search call appears under the active conversation in
traces). Does not filter results; pass ``run_id`` to filter.

agent_id.description:
Agent identifier. NOTE: memory_search is cross-agent — it
searches every agent's memories in the datapack regardless of this
value (results are scoped by datapack + user, not by agent_id), so
you will see rows written by other clients. The value is used only
for trace attribution. For naming, coding agents use
"<client>:<repo-basename>", Claude Desktop uses "claude_desktop".

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default 10).

datapack_id.description:
Optional. UUID of the datapack to search within. Defaults
to the caller's default datapack when omitted.

run_id.description:
Optional. Restricts the search to memories tagged with
this ``meko_conversation_id``. Omit for cross-conversation
results.

name: memory_update
description: Overwrite an existing memory's text by its UUID.

memory_id.description:
UUID of the memory to update. Obtain from the ``id`` field
returned by memory_search or memory_get_all — must be a valid UUID,
not an arbitrary string.

conversation_id.description: UUID from conversation_create, for trace nesting.

agent_id.description:
Agent identifier whose memory store contains this memory.
Must match the writer's `agent_id`.

name: project_add_datapack
description:
File a datapack into a project folder, or move it to a different one.

A datapack can belong to only one project, so filing one that is already
filed MOVES it rather than failing. Use ``project_describe`` to find
``folder_id``.

Needs ownership of the DATAPACK, not ownership of the project — where a
datapack lives is its owner's call. A datapack somebody shared with you
cannot be filed, and says so plainly ("only the datapack owner can change
where it is filed"), so unlike the project and folder writes there is no
not-found to misread here.

To create a datapack directly into a folder instead, pass ``folder_id`` to
``datapack_create`` — one call rather than two.

datapack_id.description: UUID of the datapack to file.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

name: project_create
description:
Create a project, optionally with its first folders.

Use this when the user asks to **create**, **add** or **start** a project
to group datapacks around one outcome.

Ask the user what the project is for before calling: the description is
what tells a later reader, and a later search, which project a piece of
work belongs in. Ask which folders they want too — a folder is one kind or
stage of work, and starting with the right two or three is easier than
reorganising later. Omitting ``folders`` gives the project the default
layout's folders, which you can change afterwards.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

description.description: What outcome the project serves. Optional but worth asking for.

folders.description: Optional folder names to create. Folders do not nest.

name: project_delete
description:
Delete a project.

The project and its folders are removed. The datapacks filed inside are
**not** deleted: they become **Unfiled** and keep working, with their
conversations, memory and knowledge untouched, and can be filed into
another project later. This deletes structure, not content.

It is still irreversible — the folder layout cannot be recovered — so
confirm with the user first, naming the project. To delete a datapack, use
``datapack_delete``.

Owner-only: a project shared with you answers "not found".

project_id.description:
UUID of the project to delete. Required — there is no
default, to avoid deleting the wrong project.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

name: project_describe
description:
Describe one project: its folders and the datapacks filed in each.

Use this when the user asks **what is in** a project, or to find which
folder a datapack sits in before moving it. This is also how to get a
``folder_id`` for ``project_add_datapack`` or ``datapack_create``.

project_id.description: UUID of the project. Use ``project_list`` to find it.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

name: project_folder_create
description:
Add a folder to a project.

Owner-only: writes to a project shared with you answer "not found", not
a permission error. Do not read that as "it does not exist" and create a
replacement — ask the owner.

A folder is one kind or stage of work. Folders do not nest. Use this when
the user asks to **add** or **create** a folder in a project.

The description is worth asking for: it is what a later knowledge or memory
search filters on when deciding which folder a new datapack belongs in, and
a folder name alone rarely says what belongs inside.

project_id.description: UUID of the project. Use ``project_list`` to find it.

folder_name.description: Name of the new folder, unique within the project.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

description.description: What belongs in the folder. Optional but worth asking for.

name: project_folder_delete
description:
Delete a folder from a project.

The folder is removed and the rest of the project is left as it is. Any
datapacks inside become **Unfiled** and keep working — this deletes
structure, not content. To delete a datapack, use ``datapack_delete``.

Owner-only: writes to a project shared with you answer "not found", not
a permission error. Do not read that as "it does not exist" and create a
replacement — ask the owner.

folder_id.description: UUID of the folder. Use ``project_describe`` to find it.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

name: project_folder_update
description:
Rename a folder, change its description, or both.

Pass only what should change; anything omitted is left alone. Use
``project_describe`` to find ``folder_id``.

Owner-only: writes to a project shared with you answer "not found", not
a permission error. Do not read that as "it does not exist" and create a
replacement — ask the owner.

folder_id.description: UUID of the folder. Use ``project_describe`` to find it.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

folder_name.description: New name. Omit to leave the name alone.

description.description:
New description. Omit to leave it alone; pass ``""`` to
clear it. Omitted and empty are different answers, which is why
this is None rather than "" by default.

name: project_list
description:
List the Meko projects the current user can see.

A project groups datapacks that work toward one outcome. Use this when the
user asks to **list**, **show** or **view** their projects, or when you
need a ``project_id`` before calling any other project tool.

The result covers projects the user owns AND projects shared with them.
Only the owner can change a shared one.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

name: project_remove_datapack
description:
Take a datapack out of its project, leaving it Unfiled.

The datapack is NOT deleted — it keeps working exactly as before, just
without a project. To delete it, use ``datapack_delete``. To move it
somewhere else instead, use ``project_add_datapack``, which moves rather
than failing.

Needs ownership of the DATAPACK, not ownership of the project it sits in
— the same rule ``project_add_datapack`` follows, because where a
datapack lives is its owner's call. A non-owner is told so plainly
("only the datapack owner can change where it is filed"), so unlike the
project and folder writes there is no not-found to misread here.

datapack_id.description: UUID of the datapack to unfile.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

name: project_stats
description:
Totals for one project: what it holds across every datapack in it.

Use this when the user asks **how much** is in a project — searches,
conversations, artifacts, indexed knowledge-base files. For the structure
rather than the totals, use ``project_describe``.

project_id.description: UUID of the project. Use ``project_list`` to find it.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

name: project_update
description:
Rename a project, change its description, or both.

Use this when the user asks to **rename** a project or to change **what it
is for**. Pass only what should change; anything omitted is left alone.
Owner-only: a project shared with you answers "not found".

project_id.description: UUID of the project. Use ``project_list`` to find it.

conversation_id.description: Langfuse conversation id from stored chat; nests the trace.

project_name.description: New name. Omit to leave the name alone.

description.description:
New description. Omit to leave it alone; pass ``""`` to
clear it. Omitted and empty are different answers, which is why
this is None rather than "" by default.

name: selflearning_query_log
description:
Read the datapack's search log: the searches that ran through ``context_search``, newest first, 10 a page.

By default only ``low`` searches (little or nothing found) are returned, since that is where fixes are. Ask
for ``mid``, ``high`` or ``all`` with ``band``, or narrow by ``reason`` or ``category``. Every row carries its
shortfall (``category``, ``reason``, ``sub_type``) and ``todos``, the ids of the to-dos it falls under.

Reasons: ``nothing_matched``, ``below_floor``, ``weak_match``, ``partial_match``, ``vague_prompt``,
``stale_source``, ``source_not_searched``, ``source_error``. Categories: ``coverage``, ``quality``, ``error``.

Pass ``log_id`` (from a row, or from ``selflearning_status`` examples) instead to read one search in full: its
ranked results with scores and what each source did.

Page with ``page``; ``has_more`` says whether another page follows. Needs the datapack's owner or maintainer
role.

datapack_id.description: UUID of the datapack. If omitted, the caller's default datapack is used.

band.description: ``low`` (default), ``mid``, ``high``, ``all``, or a comma list such as ``low,mid``.

log_id.description: UUID of one search to read in full. Ignores the other filters.

last.description: Window as ``Nd``. Default ``7d``. The log keeps about 30 days.

conversation_id.description: Conversation id from conversation_create; nests the trace.

name: selflearning_shortfalls
description:
List the distinct searches behind one to-do, with how far each has been fixed.

Take ``todo_id`` from ``selflearning_status`` (``add_context``, ``clarify_prompts``, ``refresh_sources`` or
``check_source_errors``). Each search is a distinct query, most repeated first, 10 a page, with:

- ``band``, ``best_score`` and ``reason``: how it fell short.
- ``count``: how many times it was asked.
- ``state``: ``open`` (nothing added since), ``unverified`` (something was added and no run has checked it) or
  ``verified`` (the latest replay reached ``high``).
- ``log_id``: pass it to ``selflearning_verify`` to replay it, or to ``selflearning_query_log`` to see its ranked
  results. ``test_prompt_id`` and ``latest_run`` are set once it has been saved and replayed.

Needs the datapack's owner or maintainer role.

datapack_id.description: UUID of the datapack. If omitted, the caller's default datapack is used.

last.description: Window as ``Nd``. Default is the Self-learning tab's own (14 days).

conversation_id.description: Conversation id from conversation_create; nests the trace.

name: selflearning_status
description:
Read a datapack's context quality and what to fix, as shown on its Self-learning tab.

Start here. It returns how many recent searches found a strong match (``quality``), the to-do list, and a
breakdown of the weak searches by band, shortfall category and reason. Each to-do has:

- ``id``: ``add_context``, ``clarify_prompts``, ``refresh_sources`` or ``check_source_errors`` for fixes.
- ``shortfall``: the category or reason the to-do is about (for example ``category = coverage``).
- ``searches`` and ``points``: how many searches it affects and the quality points fixing it would add.
- ``examples``: up to three of the searches behind it.

``open_fixes`` lists the fix to-dos with something to do. Read the searches behind one with
``selflearning_shortfalls``. Fix with the existing ``memory_add`` or ``knowledgebase_upload_document``, then
check it with ``selflearning_verify``. Only searches made through ``context_search`` are counted.

Needs the datapack's owner or maintainer role.

datapack_id.description: UUID of the datapack. If omitted, the caller's default datapack is used.

last.description: Window as ``Nd``, for example ``7d`` or ``30d``. Default is the Self-learning tab's own (14 days).

conversation_id.description: Conversation id from conversation_create; nests the trace.

name: selflearning_verify
description:
Replay a weak search to check that a fix worked, and report the band before and after.

Pass ``log_id`` (from ``selflearning_shortfalls`` or ``selflearning_query_log``) to save that search as a test
prompt and replay it, or ``test_prompt_id`` to replay one already saved. Use it after adding a memory or document,
not before: a replay with nothing added says so (``nothing_added_since_last_run``) and tells you nothing.

The replay runs a real search as you. It counts against your search limit, and a replay is not stored in any
conversation or counted in the datapack's search log or quality figures. A replay is also limited to 10 a
minute per user on a datapack.

A document you uploaded may still be indexing: ``indexing: true`` means the result may not include it yet, so
run again once it is false.

Needs the datapack's owner or maintainer role and a key with write scope.

datapack_id.description: UUID of the datapack. If omitted, the caller's default datapack is used.

log_id.description: UUID of a search from the log to save and replay.

test_prompt_id.description: UUID of a saved test prompt to replay. Give this or ``log_id``, not both.

conversation_id.description: Conversation id from conversation_create; nests the trace.

name: track_token_usage
description:
Record a token-usage GENERATION observation under the conversation
trace. Lets external callers (the inference gateway, future
services) attribute LLM / embedding / extraction token spend so
Meko's free-tier counters reflect real usage.

Each call writes one Langfuse generation row with ``usage =
{input, output, total}`` populated; the matching api_server query
(``SumTokenUsageByUserAndAgent``) sums them per user.

conversation_id.description:
UUID from conversation_create. Determines
which trace the observation hangs off.

name.description:
Short label for the observation — used both in the
Langfuse UI and to disambiguate token sinks in dashboards.
Recommended: "LLM Response", "LLM Summarization",
"Entity Extraction", "Embedding (KB query)",
"Embedding (conversation)".

input_tokens.description:
Prompt / input token count from the provider's
usage payload.

output_tokens.description: Completion / output token count. 0 for embeddings.

total_tokens.description:
Provider-reported total. Defaults to
input + output when omitted (matches OpenAI's convention).

model.description:
Optional model identifier (e.g. "gpt-4o-mini",
"text-embedding-3-small"). Shown in the Langfuse UI.

message_id.description:
Optional message UUID returned by
``conversation_add_message``. When provided, the
observation's metadata carries it so token spend can be
correlated to a specific turn (per-turn rollups, etc.).

datapack_id.description:
Routes to the correct tenant's Langfuse project.
Omit to use the default datapack for the request context.
